recipes.name: Toddler Muffins
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup brown sugar, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin or a 12-cup standard muffin tin.

Beat butter and brown sugar together in a mixing bowl until smooth. Stir in bananas, baby food, carrots, and eggs. Stir in flour, oat bran, baking soda, pumpkin pie spice, and salt until just combined. Spoon batter equally into the prepared muffin cups.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into centers comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely. Store at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze.

raw_recipe.headline: Toddler Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These lightly sweet muffins are made with bananas, squash, and carrots, and are perfect for picky eaters.

video.description: Even finicky toddlers love these magical mini-muffins.

review.reviewBody: Awesome! I did make a couple changes to make it even healthier still! I didn't have oat bran so I used ground flax seed. Instead of butter I used 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/4 cup vanilla yogart. 3 egg whites instead of 2 whole eggs. 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup all purpose flour. I had to cook them a few minutes longer and they turned out moist and tasty!

These were incredibly yummy. I used ~1 cup grated carrots (from baby carrots, much easier to use full-size carrots if you have them...), half a cup + 1T of steamed squash in place of the baby food jar kind, gluten free flour (bob's), a teaspoon of vanilla, and a handful of plumped raisins. I made about 12 in silicon muffin molds, and poured the rest of the batter into a small pan to bake. The pan batter got wonderfully nice and crisp, which was great–next time I'd probably make the whole thing in a sheet pan for maximum browning, since I don't have metal cupcake tins.

These are great!!! My stubborn 5yr old who refuses to eat vegetable LOVES these and has no clue they are packed with veggies!!!! I do recommend not using the baby food the recipe calls for, I purée real veggies and use that instead. It's more healthy and it's the real deal, not some processed shelf baby food. I take 1 raw yellow squash & 1 raw zucchini (with skin) and purée it in my food processor, that replaces the baby food (granted it's allot more than the 1 container it calls for, but It doesn't mess up the texture or the taste of the muffins) then I continue on with the recipe as it calls for...bananas, carrots, ect. They take more like 18-21 mins to cook and I make sure they cool on a baking rake due to being very moist cause of the extra veggies I put in them. I highly recommend these!!!!

Gorgeous recipe! So easy to adapt to ingredients on hand (great suggestions in comments). I used grated yam, apple, stone cut oats, brown sugar, and honey to taste. Peanuts, and spices: cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and cloves. Brilliant!!! Packed with a sharp cheddar and packed for after pool/gym snacks. I had googled muffin recipe for yam and apple. 🍎 I lucked out! Baked at 375f - until test stick clean, and tops golden. Baked in silicon cups. (15-20ish minutes).

So I did a few alterations based on what I had on hand. For half of the flour, I used whole wheat flour and flax seed in place of the oat bran. I also used 1 tsp baking powder and threw in half cup raisins. After cooling completely, I stored them in foil and this morning they were moist and delicious! Definitely a keeper with only 1/2 cup brown sugar in entire batch! My 2 year old grandson loves them!

5 stars for taste (not very sweet at all, which I liked) and minus 1 star for the greasy mess it made. Next time, I'll halve the butter OR use canola oil or vegetable oil. I'd increase the spice, too. The butter oozed out of the muffin and seeped into the muffin tin, making all of the bottoms wet and drippy. I had oat bran cereal and used that. I'd recommend letting the muffins sit for a few minutes before putting them into the oven so that it can hydrate. Thanks for a tasty treat!

I made this twice and it turned out great each time. The only thing I changed was I used oatmeal instead of oat bran because I didn't have any. (Oh, and the second time I used part oatmeal, part flax seed, but I think I liked the plain oatmeal better.) The first time, I used paper cupcake liners, but that didn't work very well because the bottom of the muffins came out too soggy. The next time I just greased the muffin tin with great results. I think you could definitely cut down on the sugar, especially if your bananas are ripe. I froze the second batch of these, and they freeze and reheat great. Perfect for a quick morning breakfast.

These are soooo good! I used whole wheat flour and I only had 1 banana so I used a jar of strawberry banana baby food along with the squash. I also didn't have pumpkin pie spice so I used 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp all spice and 1/4 tsp nutmeg. I didn't have enough butter so I used 1/2 coconut oil. They came out great and my 11 month old gobbles them up!! Anything to get veggies in him!!

Delicious and moist recipe. Subs: used 1/4 cup of coconut oil, 1 tsp if chia seeds, 1 cup of wheat flour and half cup of regular oats, 1/8 cup of maple syrup and didn’t have pumpkin on hand so just used a carrot apple food pouch instead. Baked for 20min

Love these muffins. I've been making them ever since my daughters were babies. Now I make them for a healthy breakfast "treat" for rushed school mornings. I love them too and I'm celiac, so I substitute Bob's Red Mill Gluten free Baking Flour 1:1, equal parts and they come out great.

Thanks for this great recipe! I have a crazy 2 year old that won't touch fruits and vegetables. I tried to get nutrition into him with smoothies at first on the recommendation of my pediatrician. Somehow he always knew what was in there and refused to drink them. Then, I came upon this recipe, and everything changed! He loves these and gobbles them up. I changed some things. I made sure I used the fine part of my grater. He would notice bigger chunks of carrots?? I used unsweetened applesauce instead of the butter. Green vegetables are the hardest for me to get him to eat, so I used an asparagus/pea medley. I was a little worried that the taste might come through with my baby food choice, but they tasted great! I used all whole wheat flour and Stevia baking blend instead of sugar. Wonderful!
Made these for my 23 month grandson. Ate one and immediately asked for another one! They are so good and healthy.

2 super small changes that didn’t need to be made, just for time sake. I use pre-shredded carrots to save time and apple sauce in place of the squash as I’m more likely to have that on hand. My (3.5yo) daughter LOVES these muffins. I forgot how many times I’ve made them for her. They also freeze really well. I keep a few out and freeze the rest. Then pop them in the microwave and they’re fresh in under a minute. Five stars!!!!

I made these muffins exactly as the recipe called for & they turned out moist and yummy. I loved that they are made with the healthy ingredients of pumpkin, bananas and carrots. I'm sure it helps the taste if your bananas are pretty brown-looking b/c bananas get sweeter that way, and mine were definitely there! I am gonna try them again as I have 2 more bananas ready to go and I wanna add more pumpkin pie spice to increase the flavor a bit more and will also try to use 1/2 wheat, 1/2 white flour.... I will update my post to let you know how they turn out!
Excellent! I have made them many times. My kids love them.
Very moist and palatable. Added fiber and vegetables are a bonus!

These are delicious and worth the time - but whoever can make these in 15 minutes needs to share how! I’ve yet to make these in under 40 minutes. Each step has other steps involved. Do yourself a favor - buy shredded carrots! And double the recipe so you can make the time it takes worth it. I freeze them and my kids love them. Just pop them in the microwave for 30 seconds to defrost. I make full size muffins and mini muffins. Enjoy!

These are definitely not just for toddlers! I used about a half cup of pumpkin in place of the baby food. Other than that I followed the recipe with wonderful results. I made 24 mini muffins for quick snacks and 6 regular size muffins. Yum!

These have become part of my Sunday afternoon routine. I bake once and we eat them throughout the week. My 1yo loves them and has been known to eat an entire regular-size muffin (or 2!) at a time. I have made the recipe as written and also with various substitutions depending on what’s on hand— apple sauce or butter-flavored shortening instead of butter, pumpkin or sweet potato instead of squash, flax seed instead of oat bran, with and without carrots, adding nuts & raisins, etc — it’s truly a little different every time. I definitely prefer these made with oat bran (cereal aisle!) as the flax meal didn’t seem to absorb as much moisture and made the muffins gluey.
I’m so happy I found this recipe!!! My son is the most picky eater, but he gobbled the muffin up and asked for more!! They are really delicious.
